chunks.arabic_text: يَحْيَىٰ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيمٍ، الْحَلَبِيُّ. رَوَىٰ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ).

translations.en: Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn 'Alim, al-Halabi. He narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Duʿafāʾ* highlights Yahyā ibn Muḥammad al-Ḥalabī, a narrator from the prominent Kufan school who transmitted directly from the Sixth Imam, al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him). His classification as 'weak' (daʿif) reflects the rigorous scrutiny applied to the chain of transmission (isnād) during the formative period of Shia hadith sciences, ensuring the authenticity of teachings attributed to the Imams. This specific evaluation underscores the importance of narrator reliability in preserving the integrity of Shia jurisprudence and theology.
en.seo_question: Who is Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn 'Alim al-Halabi and what is his status as a narrator?

key_terms.يَحْيَىٰ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيمٍ: Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn 'Alim, the narrator's name
key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Weak, a technical term in hadith sciences indicating a narrator of lower reliability
